flawed_step: 0015 (with its citation on line 0013; line 0016 fails for the same reason)
counterexample: G = S_3, H_1 = S_3, H_2 = N_2 = <(1 2)> = {e, (1 2)}. Then N_2 <| H_2 holds (a group is normal in itself), and H_1 \cap N_2 = {e, (1 2)}. But (1 3)(1 2)(1 3)^{-1} = (2 3) \notin {e, (1 2)}, so H_1 \cap N_2 is NOT normal in H_1 = S_3, contradicting the assertion of line 0015. (Taking N_1 = H_1 = S_3 <| H_1 in the same G makes the symmetric claim of line 0016 fail too: H_2 \cap N_1 = {e,(1 2)} is normal in H_2 here, so use instead H_2 = S_3, H_1 = N_1 = <(1 2)> for the mirror failure.)
reasoning_summary:
Steps 0001-0011 are fine: x_h is an arbitrary element of H_1 \cap H_2, membership in both H_1 and H_2 follows from the definition of intersection, and stating the conjugation goal plus an appeal to the Normal Subgroup Test is a legitimate plan (modulo the unstated obligation that (H_1 \cap N_2)(H_2 \cap N_1) is a subgroup contained in H_1 \cap H_2, which the proof never verifies).

The first genuine failure is line 0015 (justified on line 0013 by 'Intersection with Normal Subgroup is Normal'). That theorem states: if H \le G and N <| G, then H \cap N <| H. Its hypothesis is that N is normal in the whole ambient group. Here the hypotheses give only N_2 <| H_2, not N_2 <| G, so the theorem does not apply and the conclusion H_1 \cap N_2 <| H_1 is false in general (see counterexample). The same defect afflicts line 0016.

What is actually available is the weaker, correct statement: since N_2 \subseteq H_2, we have H_1 \cap N_2 = (H_1 \cap H_2) \cap N_2, and because H_1 \cap H_2 \le H_2 with N_2 <| H_2, the cited theorem gives H_1 \cap N_2 <| H_1 \cap H_2 (symmetrically H_2 \cap N_1 <| H_1 \cap H_2). Since the conjugating element x_h lies in H_1 \cap H_2, this weaker fact would suffice for the later manipulations on lines 0034-0039, so the theorem itself is true and the argument is repairable; but as written the proof asserts and relies on a false intermediate claim, so I stop at line 0015.

(For completeness of the audit trail: lines 0021-0031 merely insert x_h^{-1} x_h = e and then cancel it, returning to the starting expression, so they are vacuous but harmless; lines 0034 and 0037 are the substantive steps and they are the ones citing the unjustified line 0015 / 0016.)
